title: Jaguars starters not playing v. Panthers in Week 2 of preseason - Jaguars Wire
content: The Jacksonville Jaguars are not playing their starters in Week 2 of the preseason against the Carolina Panthers. This doesn't come as a surprise, but early in the week, head coach Liam Coen did leave the door open that the starters could see some action. Following the Jaguars' joint practice on Wednesday with Carolina, Coen seemed less certain, saying he wanted to watch the tape and see how Jacksonville came out of that practice injury-wise. With a joint practice scheduled each week this preseason, that is likely going to take the place of preseason action for the Jaguars' starters. Those practices provide players with new looks and a game-like setting while being in a more controlled environment. Also, unlike last year, new offensive and defensive schemes are not being implemented, so the need for preseason action this summer isn't as great. Just like last week, however, linebackers Branson Combs and Ventrell Miller are on the field as the competition for the starting role next to Foye Oluokun continues.

When he was 5 years old, David Zaid, Long Beach’s new public school superintendent, loved reading the story about the battle between David the shepherd boy who bravely defeated the giant warrior Goliath with just a simple slingshot and a stone. “It was my favorite book as a child,” Zaid said last week in an interview in his office. “It changed my life.” Zaid was born with the first name, Mynason. But he said he was so inspired by David and how he defeated Goliath that Zaid changed his name to David, and it has stuck for 46 years. Zaid, 51, said he will be remembering David’s story on the first day of school Tuesday with visits to Wilson High School to celebrate that school’s 100th anniversary and Cabrillo High School. He will follow those visits with trips to all the high schools and other schools in the district in the weeks ahead, he said. “David’s story is something that has guided me for all these years,” Zaid said. “David was old enough to have wisdom and young enough to fight. I believe that giants do fall. Regardless of the giant problems in front of us, they will fall, too.” Those giant problems facing the Long Beach school district include declining enrollment and a financial deficit. Also critical is ensuring instructional program priorities and supportive and diverse environments for students. Earlier this month, a team of reporters from the Southern California News Group, which includes the Press-Telegram, detailed that K-12 enrollment nationwide has dropped by at least 1.4 million students since pre-pandemic highs in the 2019 school year. This is especially prevalent in Orange and Los Angeles counties, where declining enrollment has outpaced the statewide average. Compared to 2015-16, the most recent school year in each county has seen enrollment drop by over 14% and 18%, respectively. Current enrollment in the Long Beach Unified School District is at 61,267, a loss of 16,371 since 2015-16. On the financial deficit, Zaid said the immediate goal is to cut about $30 million. “These issues may be difficult, but difficult doesn’t mean impossible,” he said. “Any problem can be solved as long as we do it together, as a team. Long Beach is defined by the power of its people.” Zaid said his top priority now is to listen to what parents, teachers and other school employees and community leaders and members have to say about issues facing the school district. “My number one plan is listening and then developing an action plan by January,” he said. “People want to know that their talk will lead to action. Otherwise, they get frustrated and angry.” Zaid said that he has already embarked on what he calls his “Listening and Learning Tour” to draw on “the wisdom and insights of our schools and broader community.” He said the West African Adinkra symbol of Mate Masie is helping to root him in this value. The symbol of four linked ears, originating with the Akan people of Ghana, reminds people of the importance of listening and communicating. “It means, “What I hear, I keep,” or ‘The wisdom and knowledge I collect I put in practice,” he said. As part of a recent community engagement process, seven priorities emerged, he said. Zaid is asking those he talks to what is most important to them and where would they start in dealing with these issues: –Committing to the student outcome governance model. –Ensuring safe, orderly and supportive school environments. –Strengthening student achievement and instructional programs. He also is asking the questions, “What would “early wins” be that could be attainable by June 2027 and what are we missing?” (For more information on these issues, click on lbschools.net.) David is calling his meetings, “Donuts with David. The hot light is on!” He said he was inspired by former Long Beach School Superintendent Carl Cohn’s sessions, which Cohn called, “Cookies with Carl.” Cohn was superintendent from 1992-2002. Tuesday may be Zaid’s first day as superintendent on the opening of the school year, but he is no stranger to the Long Beach school district. In fact, Long Beach is the only school district where he has served – for 32 years – after graduating from Poly High and Cal State Long Beach. He started as a teacher’s aide and then fourth and fifth-grade teacher at Lafayette Elementary followed by being principal at Stevenson Elementary. He also has worked as director of employee relations, assistant superintendent of human resource services and, most recently, assistant superintendent, elementary office. Long Beach School Board President Diana Craighead said Zaid was “a respected and student-centered leader who understands our schools and our community. The Board is confident in his ability to build on our strong foundation and continue advancing success for all students.” Zaid was born in Kaiser Permanente Hospital in Harbor City. His mother is from Mississippi, joined the Job Corps and taught English in Ethiopia where she met her husband. Hisparents returned to the United States where they have retired as social workers. Zaid spent his first five years in Long Beach, moved to Compton and graduated from Poly High in 1993. Zaid is married to his wife, Donica. They have three daughters: Zara, who is in college, and twins, Zimra and Zoie, who are in high school. Zaid said his love of education as a career started when he was in the VIP program at Poly. “I noticed that not everyone was getting the same information so I began sharing with friends,” he said. “My counselor encouraged me to go to college, which I did. I love helping students and their parents. I grew up in neighborhoods with some challenges, but I survived and set out to help others.” He earned a bachelor’s degree in psychology at Cal State Long Beach and a master’s degree in education administration from National University in 2007. He is currently pursuing his Doctor of Education in Leadership. He also has been pastor at the Seventh Day Adventist Church, The Philadelphian, on Santa Fe Avenue in Long Beach, but he said he is resigning from that position because of the additional time he will be spending in his new job as school superintendent. Zaid’s tenure as superintendent officially began July 1 and it’s been non-stop activity since. On July 16 he was honored at a reception hosted by Long Beach Mayor Rex Richardson and Long Beach City College Superintendent-President Dr. Mike Muñoz at the Maya Hotel in Long Beach. Also honored was another new education head in Long Beach, Dr. Loren J. Blanchard, who recently took over as president at California State University, Long Beach. Earlier in the day, Zaid joined these education leaders for the annual Long Beach College Promise summer retreat. It’s a long-time collaboration of Long Beach public educational institutions with the mission to make higher education accessible and equitable, guiding students from elementary school through college. Zaid credits former school superintendents – Carl Cohn, Chris Steinhauser and Jill Baker – with building a strong foundation for schools in Long Beach as “transformational leaders.” He said, “My commitment is to build on that foundation because the future of Long Beach is students sitting in our classrooms today. These students deserve a superintendent and community who will confront the challenges in front of us. Where others see fear, I see hope.” Zaid said to students, teachers, parents and community members: “I look forward to standing next to you, walking beside you and listening to you, turning those thoughts into action.” He also will be thinking about David who faced insurmountable odds but still defeated Goliath. title: NHTSA Opens Investigation Into GM V-8s That Won’t Stop Imploding, Despite Receiving Recall Remedy - Car and Driver
content:
Despite General Motors issuing a remedy for its L87 6.2-liter V-8s, NHTSA has received reports that hundreds have failed after the fix. General Motors is in hot water with the National Highway Traffic Safety Administration’s Office of Defects Investigation. The issue? Engines the automaker previously supplied with a recall fix continue to have catastrophic failures. So, the ODI team has opened a new investigation that specifically targets the L87, GM’s 6.2-liter V-8, which was the subject of recall 25V-274. The recall, which covered 597,630 trucks and SUVs in the United States, was initiated because of manufacturing defects with the crankshaft and connecting rods that could lead to a catastrophic engine failure. At the time, GM’s remedy involved engine inspections, and for units that passed scrutiny, a higher oil viscosity, a new oil fill cap, and an oil filter replacement. Those that failed were replaced. Unfortunately, neither solution seems to have fixed the underlying issue. See all results for used GMC for sale and used Cadillac for sale near 94112 The new ODI report shows that as of August 20, the office had received 499 complaints alleging post-remedy engine failures for cars affected by the recall. Of that population, 473 were supplied with a change in recommended oil while 26 received a complete engine replacement. GM itself has reported that it has received 6953 complaints of post-remedy engine failures, with the ODI reporting that it learned of a further 191 failures for engines produced outside of the recall’s production range. The oil issue has dogged GM for more than a year now. A class-action suit was brought against the company last year, alleging that the automaker knowingly sold vehicles with bad engines. Earlier this year, GM changed the recommended oil viscosity for the L87, marking the second change in recommended oil for the recalled engine. Now, the ODI is opening its investigation to include L87 engines produced outside of the production window originally laid out in the initial recall. title: Jimmy Olsen Investigates Gorilla Grodd in HBO Max’s New DCU Comedy Series - Seat42F
content: Seat42F | TV | Jimmy Olsen Investigates Gorilla Grodd in HBO Max’s New DCU Comedy Series Jimmy Olsen is getting his own corner of the DC Universe — and his first case involves a superintelligent ape accused of murder. HBO Max has ordered The People v. Gorilla Grodd, an eight-episode, half-hour comedy from DC Studios and Warner Bros. Television starring Skyler Gisondo as Jimmy Olsen and Jimmy Tatro as Gorilla Grodd. The series expands the world introduced in James Gunn’s Superman, bringing several members of the Daily Planet staff back for a very different kind of DCU story built around comedy, true crime and one of Metropolis’ most notorious murder cases. The People v. Gorilla Grodd is structured as an eight-part “true” crime docuseries produced within the DC Universe itself. Gorilla Grodd, a superintelligent ape, has been convicted of murdering his father, the King of Gorilla City. Jimmy Olsen reopens the case for the Daily Planet and begins investigating whether Grodd was wrongly convicted in one of Metropolis’ most famous murder trials. Rather than simply presenting another superhero adventure, the series is designed to feel like a documentary that could actually exist within the DCU — a Daily Planet production created for the citizens of Metropolis. Skyler Gisondo reprises his role as Jimmy Olsen after appearing as the Daily Planet photographer in Superman. He won’t be the only familiar face returning from the film. Beck Bennett will reprise his role as Steve Lombard, Mikaela Hoover returns as Cat Grant and Wendell Pierce is back as Daily Planet editor Perry White. Jimmy Tatro joins the DCU as Gorilla Grodd, the superintelligent ape at the center of Jimmy’s investigation. The cast includes Skyler Gisondo as Jimmy Olsen, Jimmy Tatro as Gorilla Grodd, Beck Bennett as Steve Lombard, Mikaela Hoover as Cat Grant and Wendell Pierce as Perry White. Additional cast members include Mary Holland, Eduardo Franco, Arian Moayed, Dan Perrault, Andrew Leeds and Tim Baltz. The People v. Gorilla Grodd comes from Tony Yacenda and Dan Perrault, the creative team behind American Vandal. Yacenda and Perrault will serve as showrunners, writers and executive producers, with Yacenda directing all eight episodes. James Gunn and Peter Safran also serve as executive producers. The combination is particularly fitting for the unusual project. American Vandal used the language and structure of serious true-crime documentaries to tell an absurd fictional mystery, while The People v. Gorilla Grodd will apply a similar approach inside the DC Universe. “We’re excited by the challenge of creating a series that feels less like an entry into the DCU and more like an artifact from it.” Yacenda and Perrault described the project as a Daily Planet original documentary made for the people of Metropolis, with the creators hoping to bring together audiences interested in comics, comedy and true crime. Gunn and Safran said the chemistry among the Daily Planet cast in Superman convinced them that the characters offered another part of the DCU worth exploring. The new series will take Jimmy beyond the Daily Planet newsroom as he investigates Metropolis’ criminal justice system and attempts to determine whether one of the city’s most infamous convicted killers belongs behind bars. HBO Max has not announced a premiere date for The People v. Gorilla Grodd. The eight-episode Max Original is produced by DC Studios in association with Warner Bros. Television. Tony Yacenda, Dan Perrault, James Gunn and Peter Safran executive produce. For more information, read HBO Max’s official announcement for The People v. Gorilla Grodd. New Gods is on the way back, and writer Ram V says there may already be an artist attached to the new volume What's next for DC's New Gods? A new series .... that may just be a revival of a recent series we just love. Writer Ram V, who wrote last year's 12-part New Gods series with artist Evan Cagle, has revealed he's not only writng another New Gods story, but he already wrote it. He describes it as "a second season/arc" from the aforementioned 2025 series, but isn't sure it they'll just pick up with a surprise New Gods #13 (well, no surprise if you're reading this!) or start it with a shining new #1. "I'm excited for everyone to see the recent New Gods thing I wrote. It's a nice check-in with all of the characters after the events of the previous arc!" V says in a League of Comic Geeks AMA. "I don't have a specific date for you all. I took a break from superheroes to do a few other things, so those are coming along nicely. That said, I worked on a New Gods thing recently and I *think* we know who the artist will be for a second season/arc!" V also states that it's unclear whether his new arc would continue the numbering of his original volume or if it will restart with a new #1, saying "the DC number-gods will decide." He does, however, offer some brief teases about what the story will entail, responding to a fan who asks whether Orion and Lightray will kiss, following their tension in his first arc. "Will they? Won't they? The foundational quandary of every good drama. First, we'll need to get Lightray back. Then, you'll have to read to find out." Alongside namechecking the work of New Gods creator Jack Kirby, a legend in the comic industry, the writer also names the manga that inspired some of his interpretation of the New Gods' abilities, which V elevated to more conceptual heights than their traditional super powers. "I wanted New Gods powers to feel a bit different to the regular superheroics of it all. Honestly, the beams and super strength / flight - all started feeling a bit generic to me," he explains. "So taking a note out of Kirby's page we thought we'd make the powers big and punchy and visually dramatic too. Of course, having read most of Bleach, The Bankai was also a big influence and on my mind!" Ram V and New Gods artist Evan Cagle recently reunited for V's creator-owned sci-fi series Deicidium. I think the new Honda HR-V needs a wing. It's a fine enough looking little crossover, and I know not to bother asking for a two-door variant, but look at the wing atop this HR-V's hatch. Are you telling me that wouldn't improve the current car, to have a little wing up there? You can tell me you think that, but you'd be wrong. I know the wing doesn't provide meaningful downforce. I know it's adding drag and decreasing economy. Adding a wing to a crossover is objectively worse, but it gives the car some character — something too many modern crossovers lack. Sometimes better things are worse, and worse things are more interesting. Wouldn't it be nice to have a crossover that didn't take itself so seriously? We had that era ever so briefly, before 9/11 killed fun and the recession drove the final nail into its coffin, but we could have it again. This is simply one of the funniest vehicles I've ever seen on Marketplace. It's a Tomos, a tiny baby moped that's meant to get you around for cheap — yet it's been done up like a full high-budget custom bike to be revealed at the Handbuilt Show. I get that there's a community around Tomos..es, but these are cheap, tiny, practical transportation. There's something hilarious about doing one up as such a beautiful build. Though, of course, maybe that's the point. Maybe the bit is that applying this level of craftsmanship to a cheap moped is funny, and this build is leaning into the absurdity. How many layers of irony are we on right now? Is this bike in on its own joke, does it understand the hilarity of its existence? Am I maybe overthinking the artistic intent behind someone in Brooklyn putting too much money into building a pretty moped? The spec of this GMC Sonoma is fascinating. The seller is upfront that the truck has an airbag-free quick-release steering wheel, the listing comes complete with a spare tire and a freshly installed clutch, but god help you if you want a driver's seat. That is NOT included, and you should feel bad for even asking. Who the hell do you think you are, asking for a driver's seat in a car you're buying? At least seats are easy to get, and once you sort out that little quirk you'll be left with a genuine race truck that you can probably put back on the street with little effort. Yeah, it's got the safety net and everything, but you can probably still just register it somewhere as a regular GMC Sonoma without the DMV asking too many questions. Just reinstall some lights first. Maybe strip off the Joker theming too — not for street legality, just for cringe. I've been on a real ute kick recently, which started with my deeply lesbian interest in Subaru Bajas being quickly soured by my years of experience owning and maintaining modified Subarus. This led to me pondering a question that scholars have debated since time immemorial: "What would the Subaru Baja be like if it was good?" Turns out, that exists, and it's the El Camino. Really it's the HSV Maloo or a Barra-powered Ford Falcon ute, but those aren't quite legal to import yet — at least, good-looking generations of the Maloo are still out of our reach. Rather than modern turbo muscle utes, we Americans will have to live with our classic V8 muscle utes for a few more years. Luckily, our old utes look incredible, and are probably a fantastic experience to own and use. This one even looks like it has a bench seat up front! Try doing that in a Baja. Some modified Subarus, though, are truly worth the effort and cash to maintain. Anything Tommykaira falls under that category, and this M20B wagon more than most. I can't say I've seen another Tommykaira'd-out wagon for sale before, they're usually all notchbacks, but this example is purported to be a genuine build. Not fake, just rare. This M20B also comes with another advantage that too few of its brethren have: It's already been imported into the U.S., and is registered and titled in the states. You don't have to deal with shipping, with import paperwork, with whatever the hell tariffs are doing right now. You can just buy this like any other Subaru, register it in your name, and have the coolest wagon anyone's ever seen. Sure, you might have to explain to all the normal people in your life why this isn't a normal thirty-year-old Subaru, but you'd probably happily do that. Look at those graphics! Surely those are worth not having electric start, right? A little leg workout never hurt anyone. The mechanical condition of this DR650 isn't quite up to the aesthetic condition, with the seller noting the clutch is near the end of its life (though a new clutch is included) and the engine bogs down when asked for high load at low RPM. It also "starts first kick when warm," which leaves the question of how many kicks the bike takes when cold. Place your bets now. If you want something easier to start, you can get your hands on my dream bike from when I was like 15 years old. I wanted an Urban Enduro so badly, and now they're just available for cheap all over the place. I've since learned what desmo maintenance actually entails and costs, and I've largely lost my appetite for Ducatis without valve springs, but maybe you're more interested in the apex of performance at all costs. I've also aged out of loving the whole militarized aesthetic of the Urban Enduro, the army green paint and the high front fender. Give me a Scrambler Icon any day, with bright vibrant colors that make you think about better things than war. If you're into the ruggedness of military equipment though, or you find the contrast of a rugged aesthetic with fragile desmo valves funny, then the bike for you is available in Brooklyn. Okay, hear me out. This is a very broken Porsche Cayenne, and it will be expensive to fix. The seller says the engine has a misfire, and that the car needs other unspecified mechanical work, but I have a pitch for you: Ignore all of that and put an LS in it. Throw a Chevy truck drivetrain in it, jack the suspension way the hell up, and romp around with the best-worst Cayenne anyone's ever had. See, despite the mechanical maladies, this Cayenne has a relatively clean body and a perfectly clean title. Use those to your advantage, and have a great time going out for a rip in the loudest, least-civilized Cayenne that money can't buy — it can only be built. I want to see an LS-powered Dakar-looking Cayenne, and I trust the Jalopnik readership to make it happen more than anyone. Build this dumb SUV, and send me photos and videos. Did you know the Ford LTD wagon of the late '80s was built on the Fox platform? I didn't, but some enterprising individual used that shared platform to their advantage in building up this longroof. On the outside it looks like any other lightly-crashed '80s Ford, with mismatched paint and aftermarket headlights, but under the hood it's all sleeper. There's a Ford 5.0 engine, bored .30 over, with a rebuilt T5 gearbox sending power to an 8.8 rear end with 4.10 gearing. Sure, the interior and exterior look like any worn-out wagon, but mechanically this thing is straight drag car. Look at the photos of the engine bay, and you'll see what I mean. That engine bay is gorgeous, perfectly clean, and even equipped with properly-working AC — I can think of few wagons I want more. I don't have $14,000 for a new car, though, so I'm forced to hope that one of you buys this and keeps it in good hands and good shape. Don't let this get wrapped around a telephone pole by some idiot kid, let it do the highway pulls it deserves for years to come.

title: The People v. Gorilla Grodd Series Coming to HBO Max - Vital Thrills
content: HBO Max has given an eight-episode, straight-to-series order for a new half-hour comedy, The People v. Gorilla Grodd, from DC Studios and Warner Bros. Television. The Max Original comedy stars Skyler Gisondo as Jimmy Olsen, Jimmy Tatro as Gorilla Grodd, and Superman actors Beck Bennett as Steve Lombard, Mikaela Hoover as Cat Grant, and Wendell Pierce as Perry White. The series also stars Mary Holland, Eduardo Franco, Arian Moayed, Dan Perrault, Andrew Leeds, and Tim Baltz. Tony Yacenda and Dan Perrault will serve as showrunners, writers, and executive producers, with Yacenda set to direct all episodes. James Gunn and Peter Safran also serve as executive producers. In The People v. Gorilla Grodd, a superintelligent ape is convicted of murdering his father, the King of Gorilla City. In an eight-part “true” crime docuseries, the Daily Planet’s Jimmy Olsen reopens the case, investigating whether Gorilla Grodd was wrongly convicted in one of Metropolis’ most famous murder trials. “We are thrilled to be working with Tony and Dan, alongside James, Peter, the entire DC team and our colleagues at WBTV, to bring these iconic DCU characters to HBO Max in a new and unexpected way,” said Amy Gravitt, Executive Vice President, HBO Programming, Head of HBO & HBO Max Comedy Series. “We already know Skyler Gisondo is pitch-perfect as Jimmy Olsen and we can’t wait for fans to experience Jimmy Tatro’s captivating and hilarious portrayal of Grodd.” James Gunn and Peter Safran, executive producers and DC Studios’ Co-Chairmen & Co-CEOs, added: “Between Skyler’s wonderful performance and the fantastic chemistry of the Daily Planet cast, we knew coming out of ‘Superman’ that this would be a fun world to explore. “We’re excited to work with the brilliant Dan Perrault and Tony Yacenda to take the audience down some of the darker and funnier streets and alleyways of the DCU as Jimmy spotlights the Metropolis criminal justice system for his docuseries.” Tony Yacenda and Dan Perrault, showrunners, writers, and executive producers, commented: “We’re excited by the challenge of creating a series that feels less like an entry into the DCU and more like an artifact from it. A Daily Planet original documentary made for the people of Metropolis. “We hope it’ll appeal to fans of the comics, comedy and true crime. And while we can’t speak for audiences here yet, we already know it’s a huge hit in Metropolis. title: HBO Max Greenlights THE PEOPLE V. GORILLA GRODD Comedy Series - Nerdist
content: We’ve been hearing about an HBO show about Jimmy Olsen and Gorilla Grodd from DC Studios for almost a year now, with various titles given. One of them was DC Crime, which James Gunn later debunked. Well, at last, we have not only a name for the series, The People v. Gorilla Grodd, but we officially have a full season order from HBO Max. The series consists of eight episodes, and HBO describes it as a half-hour comedy series. Skyler Gisondo will reprise his role as Jimmy Olsen from Superman, with Jimmy Tatro playing Gorilla Grodd. Tony Yacenda and Dan Perrault, creators of Netflix’s American Vandal, will serve as showrunners, writers, and executive producers, with Yacenda directing all episodes. A superintelligent ape is convicted of murdering his father, the King of Gorilla City. In an eight-part “true” crime docuseries, the Daily Planet’s Jimmy Olsen reopens the case, investigating whether Gorilla Grodd was wrongly convicted in one of Metropolis’ most famous murder trials. Right now, the series will star several Superman cast members, including Beck Bennett as Steve Lombard, Mikaela Hoover as Cat Grant, and Wendell Pierce as Perry White. The series also stars Mary Holland, Eduardo Franco, Arian Moayed, Dan Perrault, Andrew Leeds, and Tim Baltz. From the looks of it, David Corenswet’s Clark Kent and Rachel Brosnahan’s Lois Lane won’t appear, but they could always make a surprise cameo. Our real question as DC fans is if any other major DC Comics heroes appear. Especially if Superman is not the hero who fought and captured Gorilla Grodd. Specifically, we’re wondering if the Flash is going to pop up. But we’d love to see any DC hero. Somehow, we have a feeling Nathan Fillion as Green Lantern Guy Gardner will appear. He seems to be the DCU’s lucky charm. No premiere date was given, but we would be surprised to see it before 2028.

HBO Max has handed the half-hour Max Original an eight-episode, straight-to-series order, and the premise sounds like it could be one of the strangest and funniest corners of the DCU yet. Previously developed under the title DC Crime, the series stars Skyler Gisondo as Jimmy Olsen, who turns investigative documentarian to examine one of Metropolis' most notorious murder cases. Jimmy Tatro will play Gorilla Grodd, who has been convicted of murdering his own father, the King of Gorilla City. The story unfolds as an eight-part "true" crime documentary created within the DCU. Jimmy reopens Grodd's case and starts investigating whether the superintelligent ape was actually responsible for the murder that put him behind bars. They also released an in-universe press release that offers additional details about what Grodd allegedly did. He isn't simply accused of killing his father. He's also accused of consuming his father's brain. That's one hell of a case for Jimmy Olsen to tackle. Several familiar faces from Superman will join Gisondo in the series. Beck Bennett returns as Steve Lombard, Mikaela Hoover is back as Cat Grant, and Wendell Pierce once again plays Daily Planet editor Perry White. The rest of the cast includes Mary Holland, Eduardo Franco, Arian Moayed, Dan Perrault, Andrew Leeds, and Tim Baltz, although DC Studios hasn't revealed their characters yet. Tony Yacenda and Perrault will serve as showrunners, writers, and executive producers, with Yacenda directing all eight episodes. James Gunn and Peter Safran are also executive producing the series for DC Studios. Gunn and Safran explained that the Daily Planet crew's dynamic in Superman helped convince them that these characters deserved another story: "Between Skyler’s wonderful performance and the fantastic chemistry of the Daily Planet cast, we knew coming out of 'Superman' that this would be a fun world to explore." They added: "We're excited to work with the brilliant Dan Perrault and Tony Yacenda to take the audience down some of the darker and funnier streets and alleyways of the DCU as Jimmy spotlights the Metropolis criminal justice system for his docuseries," Yacenda and Perrault are approaching the project from an especially cool angle. Rather than making a traditional DC comedy that happens to use a documentary format, they want The People v. Gorilla Grodd to feel like something that was actually produced and released inside the DCU. They explained: "We’re excited by the challenge of creating a series that feels less like an entry into the DCU and more like an artefact from it. A Daily Planet original documentary made for the people of Metropolis." They continued: "We hope it’ll appeal to fans of the comics, comedy and true crime, And while we can’t speak for audiences here yet, we already know it’s a huge hit in Metropolis. They love this series." That's a great way to expand this universe. Instead of every DCU project needing to revolve around another giant superhero conflict, The People v. Gorilla Grodd gets to explore what entertainment and journalism might look like for ordinary people living in a world filled with superheroes, alien invasions, talking apes, and bizarre crimes. Amy Gravitt, Executive Vice President, HBO Programming, Head of HBO & HBO Max Comedy Series, also shared her enthusiasm for the project: "We are thrilled to be working with Tony and Dan, alongside James, Peter, the entire DC team and our colleagues at WBTV, to bring these iconic DCU characters to HBO Max in a new and unexpected way." Gravitt also offered a tease of what Tatro is bringing to one of DC's most famous villains: "We already know Skyler Gisondo is pitch-perfect as Jimmy Olsen, and we can’t wait for fans to experience Jimmy Tatro’s captivating and hilarious portrayal of Grodd." Turning Gorilla Grodd into the subject of an in-universe true-crime documentary is such a ridiculous idea that it has plenty of potential. Pairing him with Gisondo's Jimmy Olsen makes it even more interesting, especially with the Daily Planet characters from Superman returning around him. One major DC character hasn't been mentioned, though. There's currently nothing indicating that The Flash will appear in The People v. Gorilla Grodd. Grodd is traditionally one of the Scarlet Speedster's greatest enemies in the comics, but this story appears focused on Grodd's murder conviction, Jimmy's investigation, and the Metropolis criminal justice system rather than his superhero rivalry. The People v. Gorilla Grodd doesn't have an official HBO Max premiere date yet, though a 2028 launch currently looks likely. A Gorilla Grodd murder trial presented as a Daily Planet true-crime documentary isn't something I expected from the DCU, but I'm absolutely curious to see how weird this gets. title: 'The People v. Gorilla Grodd' Cast, Plot, And Release Window For The DCU'S Wildest Spinoff - Inverse
content: The Jimmy Olsen TV series might be more important than anyone realizes. Even after 18 years, DC Comics and Warner Bros. haven’t replicated the reliable output of the Marvel Cinematic Universe, but it sure seems like James Gunn is determined to strong-arm this newest attempt into success. Since becoming co-CEO of DC Studios back in 2022, Gunn has constructed an ambitious Chapter One of the burgeoning DC Universe franchise on-screen, with plans to introduce new versions of Batman (separate from Matt Reeves’ incarnation) and Wonder Woman in solo films while also making room for smaller projects like the upcoming Clayface. The critical and commercial success of last year’s Superman felt like a solid foundation to build on, but this summer’s box office failure of Supergirl throws everything into question. But one struggling movie isn’t going to stop such an expensive locomotive, and there are still a lot more DC Universe projects coming, including the Superman sequel Man of Tomorrow and Lanterns, a TV adaptation of the Green Lantern mythos. There are also numerous spin-offs in the works, from a TV show about Superman MVP Mr. Terrific to an animated retelling of Tom King’s Mister Miracle comic book miniseries. The most surprising of these shows is the untitled Jimmy Olsen series, and it’s the one that just picked up the most steam with an unexpected casting announcement. On August 21, 2026, the Jimmy Olsen spinoff received its official title and green light: The People v. Gorilla Grodd. The series is an eight-episode half-hour comedy following Superman breakout Jimmy Olsen (Skyler Gisondo) as he reopens a murder-mystery case involving Gorilla Grodd. The series is executive produced by James Gunn, Peter Safran, Tony Yacenda, and Dan Perrault. Yacenda and Perrault also serve as showrunners and writers. Per HBO, all episodes will be directed by Tony Yacenda. Skyler Gisondo’s Jimmy Olsen will take the lead of a spin-off show. With the announcement of the show’s green light, HBO revealed its cast list of returning Superman veterans and new cast members. The series also stars Mary Holland, Eduardo Franco, Arian Moayed, Dan Perrault, Andrew Leeds, and Tim Baltz in yet-unannounced roles. With the announcement of the show, HBO revealed a logline for The People v. Gorilla Grodd: HBO also released a cheeky news bulletin from The Daily Planet, revealing more of the in-world context in which The People v. Gorilla Grodd takes place. The series  will be modeled after a true-crime docuseries hosted by Olsen, presumably in the vein of Netflix’s American Vandal, the creators of which have been confirmed as showrunners). This approach seems to be confirmed by the statement from DC Studios co-chiefs James Gunn and Peter Safran, who said, “Between Skyler’s wonderful performance and the fantastic chemistry of the Daily Planet cast, we knew coming out of ‘Superman’ that this would be a fun world to explore.  We're excited to work with the brilliant Dan Perrault and Tony Yacenda to take the audience down some of the darker and funnier streets and alleyways of the DCU as Jimmy spotlights the Metropolis criminal justice system for his docuseries.” If the show makes it to a second season, there’s the possibility that it could function like an anthology series, with a focus on a new case every year. For those unsure as to why a Jimmy Olsen spinoff has been ordered so early in the DCU’s lifespan, it might be its potential to introduce new corners of the DC Universe before we get a project like The Flash to properly flesh them out. There isn’t a trailer for the upcoming Jimmy Olsen mocku-series yet, as the show has just begun filming. We’ll update this page with more information when a trailer does drop. Gorilla Grodd is one of The Flash’s best-known antagonists, and his presence could hint at the hero’s coming arrival. There’s no release date yet, but considering the show is set to begin filming later this year, it’s a safe assumption that it’ll air sometime in 2027. Warner Bros. has been trying to get a cinematic DC Universe off the ground for years now, and aside from the short-lived Snyderverse, this has been its strongest attempt. With the back-to-back releases of Superman and Supergirl establishing the Kryptonian status quo, and other films like The Brave and the Bold and an untitled Wonder Woman film already in motion, it’s clear that Gunn is moving fast to establish the franchise’s other tentpole foundations. Although a Jimmy Olsen spinoff show feels like a strange move from the outside looking in, it may be a clever way to tease characters fans might not expect to see for some time. title: We Test Chevy’s New Small-Block V-8 in the 2027 Corvette Grand Sport - Car and Driver
content: The new 6.7-liter LS6 gives the Vette more oomph and puts its 60-mph time between the LT2-equipped Stingray and the Z06. Welcome to Car and Driver's Testing Hub, where we zoom in on the test numbers. We've been pushing vehicles to their limits since 1956 to provide objective data to bolster our subjective impressions (you can see how we test here). If the Grand Sport’s return to the Corvette lineup wasn’t exciting enough, it also marks the debut of GM’s sixth-generation small-block V-8. And this power couple is our first opportunity to test the beastly 6.7-liter version of that engine at the test track. Naturally, that’s big news, so we’re highlighting the 2027 Chevy Corvette GS’s acceleration times, with our $142,380 3LT-spec test car notably featuring the $10,995 carbon-fiber wheels and the Z52 Track Performance package ($20,695) that includes carbon-ceramic brakes, a more aggressive aero configuration, and ultra-sticky Michelin Pilot Sport Cup 2R tires. See all results for new 2027 Chevrolet Corvette Stingray / Grand Sport for sale near 94112 For the 2027 model year, both the Stingray and the Grand Sport share the same LS6 engine, with the naturally aspirated V-8 producing 535 horsepower and 520 pound-feet of torque. Those figures represent increases of 40 horses and 50 pound-feet versus the outgoing LT2 6.2-liter V-8. Once again, an eight-speed dual-clutch automatic feeds the rear wheels, with the Grand Sport alone inheriting a shorter 5.56:1 final-drive ratio from the racier 670-hp Corvette Z06. Like before, the GS also adopts wider bodywork from the most hardcore Vettes, and—unlike the Stingray—it can be equipped with the aforementioned Z52 Track pack. So, what did all of this mean once we got the C8 Grand Sport to our test track? Well, the sprint to 60 mph took 2.7 seconds. Compared with a 2026 Stingray Z51 that we tested, the GS was two-tenths quicker to the mile-per-minute mark; it was also only 0.1 second behind a Z06 coupe with the track-spec Z07 package we tested. After a few more seconds of this new V-8 screaming, the Grand Sport completed the quarter-mile in 11.0 seconds, with a trap speed of 123 mph. The quickest 495-hp Stingray needed 11.2 ticks at 122 mph, whereas the Z06 did the deed in 10.5 seconds at 131 mph. It’s not news that Corvettes can stop on a dime and corner like the “Quad God” Ilia Malinin. Still, we run our full battery of tests on every new vehicle, whether it’s a humble Hyundai Venue or a new six-figure Grand Sport. The latter certainly benefited from its racetrack-ready rubber, which helped haul our 3688-pound test car to a stop from 70 mph in 144 feet and from 100 mph in 286 feet, in line with other C8s wearing Cup 2Rs. It also posted 1.18 g on our 300-foot skidpad, which is the best C8 cornering result we’ve measured, surpassing the Z06 (1.16 g), ZR1X (1.14 g), and ZR1 (1.13 g). For those of you who were wondering, a manual C7 Grand Sport with the Z07 package recorded a 123-foot stop from 70 mph and 1.18 g of max cornering grip in our testing. Tatro starred in the first season of the Netflix series. “Between Skyler’s wonderful performance and the fantastic chemistry of the Daily Planet cast, we knew coming out of Superman that this would be a fun world to explore,” said DC Studios heads James Gunn and Peter Safran. “We’re excited to work with the brilliant Dan Perrault and Tony Yacenda to take the audience down some of the darker and funnier streets and alleyways of the DCU as Jimmy spotlights the Metropolis criminal justice system for his docuseries.” Said Amy Gravitt, executive vp HBO Programming and head of HBO & HBO Max comedy series, “We are thrilled to be working with Tony and Dan, alongside James, Peter, the entire DC team and our colleagues at WBTV, to bring these iconic DCU characters to HBO Max in a new and unexpected way. We already know Skyler Gisondo is pitch-perfect as Jimmy Olsen, and we can’t wait for fans to experience Jimmy Tatro’s captivating and hilarious portrayal of Grodd.” As part of the series announcement, HBO Max offered up a mock Daily Planet press release touting Olsen’s documentary. It includes this quote from Pierce’s Perry White: “Everyone thinks they know Grodd: the power-hungry gorilla who killed his father for the throne of Gorilla City. But once you start to look beneath the fur, you start to realize there’s a lot more to that primate.” The series order for The People v. Gorilla Grodd comes on the heels of DC Studios’ Lanterns scoring positive reviews and a big audience for its Aug. 16 series premiere. Lanterns has a considerably darker tone than the one the new series will shoot for. “We’re excited by the challenge of creating a series that feels less like an entry into the DCU and more like an artifact from it, a Daily Planet original documentary made for the people of Metropolis,” said Yacenda and Perrault. “We hope it’ll appeal to fans of the comics, comedy and true crime. And while we can’t speak for audiences here yet, we already know it’s a huge hit in Metropolis. They love this series.” Yacenda and Perrault are executive producing with Gunn and Safran; Yacenda will also direct every episode. Warner Bros. Television is the studio. title: Hull City v Man Utd: Key stats and talking points - Yahoo Sports
content: Hull City kick off a first Premier League campaign in nearly a decade by taking on 13-time winners Manchester United. BBC Sport examines some of the key themes going into the meeting at the MKM Stadium on Saturday. The Tigers are the first side to be promoted to the Premier League after finishing sixth in the Championship since Blackpool in 2010, having defeated Millwall and then Middlesbrough in the play-offs. Hull boss Sergej Jakirovic - the first Bosnian Premier League manager - will take on the challenge of keeping the newly promoted side in the top flight and to do so he may need to develop Hull's style of play. Despite triumphing in the play-off final in May, Hull's underlying numbers last season were not those of an elite outfit. They had the fifth-fewest shots of any second-tier team in 2025-26, while only bottom club Sheffield Wednesday had a higher tally of expected goals against. Hull also faced the third-most shots (681), an unwelcome set of statistics that underline the club's status as favourites to return to the Championship. Hull, though, can take some solace from a solid opening-day record in the Premier League. They have triumphed in three of their five opening matches in the competition, defeating reigning champions Leicester City on their most recent appearance in 2016. This time round the Tigers take on a United team who have won their opening Premier League fixture on an unrivalled 22 occasions. Carrick's men, boosted by new signings including midfielders Youri Tielemans and Andrey Santos, are facing promoted sides in their first two matches, with a home game against Ipswich Town to come, providing the Red Devils the perfect opportunity for a strong start following their third-place finish last season. Carrick has won four of his six managerial meetings with Hull (D1, L1) and is unbeaten in three visits to the MKM Stadium (W2, D1). United's manager will also be hoping that the form of Bruno Fernandes continues into this campaign as the club return to Champions League football. The club captain set a record for most assists in a Premier League campaign last season with 21, along with scoring nine goals – making Fernandes the first United player to be involved in 30 or more goals in two Premier League seasons.

title: Cadillac debuts stunning 830HP V-ONE concept inspired by its Le Mans racer and its cockpit is jaw dropping - supercarblondie.com
content:
Published on Aug 21, 2026 at 10:07 PM (UTC+4)
								by Ben Thompson Last updated on Aug 21, 2026 at 10:07 PM (UTC+4)
								Edited by
								Mason Jones Cadillac has debuted a V-ONE concept car inspired by its Le Mans racer. Capable of 830hp, the car is decked out in a stunning day-to-night coloring. Described as the ‘ultimate manifestation of a customer performance concept’, the V-ONE got its moment to shine at Monterey Car Week. And the Supercar Blondie team was there to get a closer look. Monterey Car Week has come and gone, with another spectacular lineup of cars. From the $4 million Koenigsegg CCGT1 to  1-of-150 Aston Martin Valen, and the $2 million Czinger 21C Spyder, there’s been a lot tot take in for the Supercar Blondie team. Joining those ranks is the Cadillac V-ONE concept car. The V-ONE is co-developed by Cadillac Design, Cadillac Racing and chassis constructor Dallara to deliver ‘factory-level prototype performance and technology’. At the heart of this car is a V8 hybrid powertrain, sharing foundations with the Cadillac V-Series.R race car. Beyond the engine, the concept shares architectural touches like suspension, transmission, and select electronics. On the outside too, this car remains faithful to the V-Series.R, while also incorporating refined details. The hand-sprayed paint gradient represents a day-to-night transition, as it fades from silver to deep navy. But it’s the cockpit that’s the real knockout here. The steering wheel inside this car was an instant eye-catcher. Chloe, the presenter taking a look at the car, noticed this straight away. “There’s also a flicky switch over that, that is brake bias. This cockpit is racing style-inspired.” What is brake bias? It’s when braking force is split between a car’s front and rear wheels. Bias towards the front makes the car more stable, while bias towards the rear assists in turning. On one of the doors is a plaque that reads ‘Hand-built in Detroit’. “Something about that feels so official,” Chloe commented. As if that wasn’t cool enough, the V-ONE also had a custom painted helmet which matched the car. The car was on display on The Quail on August 14, and all we can say is that everyone who got to see it on the day was extremely lucky. title: Ruth B. Has Made Her Peace - V Magazine
content: From ‘Lost Boy’ to ‘Dandelions,’ Canadian singer Ruth B. looks back on the internet hits that shaped her, and the healing process that inspired her next chapter From ‘Lost Boy’ to ‘Dandelions,’ Canadian singer Ruth B. looks back on the internet hits that shaped her, and the healing process that inspired her next chapter The year is 2015, and everyone wears combat boots, abides by quirky Pinterest quotes, and posts on the biggest short-form video app, Vine. For over a year, 19-year-old Ruth Berhe (B for short) from Edmonton—the capital of the Canadian province of Alberta—had been uploading covers of herself singing and playing keyboard from her childhood bedroom. Then inspiration struck in the form of a Once Upon a Time episode, and Berhe published a six-second clip of herself playing four very satisfying chords while singing: “I am a lost boy from Neverland, usually hanging out with Peter Pan.” Suddenly people were demanding a full song, which she released in full on YouTube. “Lost Boy” became a multi-platinum hit, garnering nearly 200 million views on YouTube, peaking at No. 24 on the Billboard Hot 100, and earning Berhe a record deal. In a rare feat, Ruth B. joined the ranks of Justin Bieber, Shawn Mendes, Halsey, and Alessia Cara as a musician discovered via social media in the 2010s. “The internet is such a great tool to share your music… you never know who’s gonna hear you,” Berhe says. The singer views her relationship with her fans as a collaborative one. Fresh off earning a deal with Columbia Records, she kept posting on Vine as fans prompted her to keep expanding her catalog. Eventually, Ruth B. debuted her first studio album, Safe Haven, which she credits to her hometown of Edmonton and to her parents, with whom she lived until her late twenties. Despite the massive success of “Lost Boy,” Safe Haven didn’t make much noise when it was originally released in 2017. But the album includes one of the first songs Berhe ever wrote, “Dandelions,” a whimsical love song that made a huge resurgence at the start of the pandemic in the most unlikely of places: Indonesia. New to TikTok in 2020, the singer was scrolling the app when she noticed “Dandelions” being used by someone on the other side of the world. In early 2021, the song made its way to North America, where it gained traction after fans independently created a slowed-and-reverbed version. Berhe embraced the trend, officially releasing the remix that summer. By 2022, “Dandelions” had become a global viral sensation, used in over 2.6 million TikTok videos and accumulating more than 2 billion streams on Spotify alone. Its romantic, dream-like melody and lyrics have made it a go-to for first dances. Berhe even re-recorded a special piano version of “Dandelions” for her best friend’s wedding—a moment that left the singer emotional as she watched the couple share their first dance to her own song. Fast-forward to the summer of 2026: Berhe now lives in Los Angeles, where she has built her highly anticipated third album, Peace To Make, due out worldwide on Friday, August 21. The album grew out of a period of transition in the singer’s life. Having just come out of a long relationship, Berhe leaned on her love of songwriting to work through her emotions. “I knew this had to be me genuinely processing this relationship being over and this new life I was living in,” she says. Once she had drafts of “Best Days” and “Bad Combination,” Berhe brought the songs to Cole M.G.N. (Cole Marsden Greif-Neill), who serves as the main producer on Peace To Make, and the two knew they could make an album together. They started from the ground up: M.G.N. would experiment with melodies while Berhe felt out the music and wrote about the many emotions surfacing at specific moments of her growth. “A big part of why I’ve healed and moved on from those emotions was because of this album and being able to write it, so that makes it much more special to me.” Needless to say, Ruth B.’s third record was truly her “peace to make.” Working with a single producer let Berhe get out of her head. She recalls the day she worked on “Breathe” in the studio, where M.G.N. encouraged her to start singing rather than writing while he played along. At first she mumbled a lot of “la, la, la’s,” but the moment M.G.N. played what she calls “the most beautiful guitar I’d ever heard in my life,” the hook clicked into place, and the two shared a jolt of collaborative excitement. In more ways than one, “Breathe” is the track that became the catharsis of Berhe’s healing. The song took a year to finish, she reveals, because she hit a wall and went home to Edmonton for six months to process her trajectory as an artist. “Genuinely from the beginning of ‘Lost Boy,’ my life took off so quick that I never had a minute to sit [with everything].” After a few months of therapy, Berhe decided to take a solo trip to Banff, the mountain town she used to visit growing up. Connecting with nature, she reconnected with herself—and finally found the space to finish “Breathe.” The closing lyrics go, “The mountains are so big, I feel so small. The oceans are so great, they could drown me if they want.” In that moment, Berhe found comfort in realizing “nothing is really that big.” One spine-tingling song that deserves to be a hit on Peace To Make is “Didn’t I,” written while Berhe was hanging out with friends in the music industry. She tells me she doesn’t normally break into song around friends—but, as she puts it, “when there’s some wine involved, you’re just fearless.” In a friend’s studio, she found her inspiration as someone played around with instrumentals, and she asked for a mic. She started by singing the phrase “Didn’t I” over and over in a wine-loosened haze, then finished the whole song in about 45 minutes—a whirlwind she “didn’t think anything of” at the time. The next morning, she casually sent the draft to her manager, who told her to pass it along to the label. Another Ruth B. banger was born. It’s been nearly four years since Berhe last performed live for her own fans. Over the past few months, she’s been reconnecting with them through social media. For starters, she wiped her entire Instagram feed, rebranding to launch the official Peace To Make era. She’s also been posting more consistently on TikTok, dropping singles like “Bad Combination” and “Didn’t I” and teasing snippets of new material. Berhe hopes fans feel understood by this album and treat it as “a safe place to go when you’re hurting or healing.” In the past, she would linger after her shows to talk with fans about how her music had changed their lives for the better. She’s looking forward to more of those enlightening, cathartic conversations—especially hearing about listeners’ own introspective journeys with the new album. The closing track on Peace To Make is “Pick Me,” a title that flips its usual meaning: it’s about ending a relationship and realizing the best thing you can do is choose yourself. In a relationship, Berhe says, she tends to be an empath, someone who struggles to see the bad in people. But “Pick Me” captures the season she’s in now: “knowing my worth, knowing what I deserve, and not settling for anything less than that.” We are using cookies to give you the best experience on our website. title: NHTSA Expands Probe Into 997,000 GM V-8 Trucks and SUVs After Reported Post-Recall Engine Failures - Road & Track
content: NHTSA is looking into reported post-recall engine failures affecting GM’s 6.2-liter V-8 trucks and SUVs. On Thursday, the National Highway Traffic Safety Administration's (NHTSA) Office of Defects Investigation (ODI) announced it has opened an engineering analysis investigation regarding continued consumer complaints surrounding post-remedy engine failures in vehicles powered by General Motors’s 6.2-liter V-8 engine, known internally as the L87. ODI has broadened the scope of its investigation beyond that covered in Recall 25V-274, with it spanning a potential pool of 997,743 GM products. The new investigation comes after ODI received 499 complaints in which consumers reported post-remedy engine failure in their vehicles after receiving the repairs mandated in Recall 25V-274. This recall involved 2021–2026 GM vehicles equipped with the 6.2-liter L87 V-8 engine, which General Motors says were impacted by supplier manufacturing and quality issues. These include popular models like the Chevrolet Silverado, Suburban, and Tahoe, Cadillac’s Escalade, and GMC’s Sierra and Yukon. In other words, some of GM’s best-sellers—and most important profit drivers. General Motors had taken a two-pronged approach to that recall, stating that customers would either receive a different viscosity oil or a total engine replacement based on the results of a dealer inspection. A total of 473 ODI complaints claimed that their engine failure came after the change in oil, while 26 had received a full engine replacement before another failure occurred.  Furthermore, ODI has also received an additional 191 complaints of L87 engines not covered by the original recall failing. NHTSA reports that GM reported receiving 6953 complaints of post-remedy engine failure as well. As a result, ODI will now begin to investigate L87 engines built after the March 1, 2021 to May 31, 2024 timeline covered by Recall 25V-274. With GM now offering a next-gen small block in both 5.7-liter and 6.7-liter capacities, it wouldn’t be surprising to see the L87 phased out of its current roles sooner rather than later. title: FTC v. Illinois: Federal and State Disparate-Impact Policies Continue to Diverge - JD Supra
content:
Federal agencies and states are increasingly taking divergent approaches to disparate-impact liability. While the federal government has moved to eliminate disparate-impact enforcement, several states have taken steps to preserve or expand liability based on discriminatory effects. Most recently, on August 7, the FTC announced a policy statement providing that it will no longer pursue disparate-impact claims under any statute it enforces and will no longer bring antidiscrimination claims under Section 5 of the FTC Act. The FTC stated that neither Section 5 nor the Equal Credit Opportunity Act (ECOA) authorizes disparate-impact claims. Under the new policy, the Commission will continue to pursue disparate-treatment claims under ECOA where the facts support intentional discrimination, but it will not pursue liability based solely on a policy’s differential effects. The FTC also modified certain compliance obligations arising from prior auto-dealer matters involving statistical analyses associated with disparate-impact theories. The FTC’s actions come on the heels of an April 2025 executive order directing agencies to curtail disparate-impact enforcement (previously discussed here). At the state level, however, regulators and legislatures have taken steps to preserve or expressly establish disparate-impact standards (See our discussion of New Jersey here.) On July 31, Illinois enacted the Civil Rights Safeguard Act, which takes effect January 1, 2027 and expressly incorporates an effects-based discrimination standard into the Illinois Human Rights Act. For financial institutions, the Act prohibits the use of lending criteria or methods that have the effect of subjecting individuals to unlawful discrimination where the practice is not necessary to achieve a substantial, legitimate, nondiscriminatory interest or that interest could be served through another practice with a less discriminatory effect. The Illinois amendments define “criteria or methods” to include practices, policies, and groups of practices or policies. They also apply the new standard to persons offering credit cards to the public and permit the Illinois Department of Human Rights to consult with state or federal financial regulators when investigating a charge involving a financial institution. These developments reflect a widening divide over the role of disparate-impact liability in fair lending. While federal agencies are retreating from effects-based theories, states may continue to adopt or preserve their own standards, creating different substantive requirements across jurisdictions. Putting It Into Practice: The divergent approaches in state and federal disparate impact liability leave financial institutions facing substantially different fair lending expectations depending on the applicable jurisdiction. Financial institutions should therefore continue assessing fair lending compliance on a state-by-state basis notwithstanding the federal pullback. title: Newcastle v Liverpool | Matthias Jaissle | Pre Match Press Conference - Yahoo Sports
content: Newcastle United head coach Matthias Jaissle has addressed the media ahead of his first competitive match in charge of the club, with Liverpool preparing to visit St James' Park on Sunday afternoon. The Premier League opener represents the beginning of a new era on Tyneside, with Jaissle replacing Eddie Howe and taking charge of a Newcastle squad that has undergone significant changes during the summer. The German head coach admitted that his team is still a work in progress, but insisted that supporters should expect an aggressive, high-intensity style of football. Jaissle is clearly aware of the scale of the challenge facing him. Newcastle have lost several influential players during the summer, including Bruno Guimaraes, Sandro Tonali and Anthony Gordon, while the club has also had to integrate a number of younger additions into the first-team squad. Rather than focusing on what has been lost, however, Jaissle has repeatedly called for unity and positivity. Ahead of his first competitive fixture, he urged supporters to believe in the project and continue providing the backing that has traditionally made St James' Park such a difficult place for visiting teams. "I'm excited. I am looking forward to it. First match at home. It will be sold out. It is an amazing privilege to be head coach of Newcastle United," Jaissle said ahead of Sunday's encounter. The manager also provided an important injury update. Tino Livramento has returned to partial group training after his World Cup-related injury, but Jaissle confirmed that the defender will not be rushed back into action. The Newcastle boss explained that the club needs to be smart with Livramento's rehabilitation and wait until he is completely ready. Joelinton is another confirmed absentee. The midfielder is expected to be unavailable for several weeks, creating another selection problem for Jaissle as he prepares for his first Premier League fixture. There was more positive news surrounding Amar Dedić, however. The versatile defender has worked with Jaissle previously and already understands many of the tactical demands expected from his new manager. With Livramento unavailable, Dedić appears set to play an important role for Newcastle against Liverpool. "Amar is a perfect addition to the squad," Jaissle explained, highlighting the benefit of their previous relationship and Dedić's versatility. Sunday's fixture will also provide an immediate test of Jaissle's footballing philosophy. The 38-year-old wants Newcastle to play with intensity, aggression and courage, while maintaining an identity that supporters can recognise. However, he has acknowledged that transforming the team will take time, particularly given the late appointment and extensive changes to the squad. Liverpool will provide an especially demanding first opponent. They finished fifth last season and arrive under new manager Andoni Iraola, who is also attempting to implement a high-energy, aggressive style of football. For Newcastle, therefore, this is about more than simply collecting three points. It is the first competitive opportunity for Jaissle to demonstrate what his Newcastle can become. With a sold-out St James' Park behind him, the new head coach will hope his players can respond with the intensity, togetherness and belief that he has demanded throughout pre-season. The Premier League opener takes place at St James' Park on Sunday, August 23, with kick-off scheduled for 4:30pm BST. After a turbulent summer, the wait is almost over. The Jaissle era is ready to begin.

title: Hyundai's Ioniq V Looks Like A Lambo, Is As Big As A Camry, And Costs Less Than America's Cheapest New Car - Carscoops
content:
At 193 inches long for Venue money, this cyberpunk electric sedan makes Western EV pricing hard to defend When Hyundai launched the original Ioniq Hybrid in America in 2017, it started at $22,200. Almost a decade later, Chinese buyers can order an entirely new, fully electric Ioniq sedan for less. The wedgy Ioniq V has entered pre-sales at just 119,900 yuan, which equates to only $17,800 at current exchange rates. That’s nearly $3,000 less than the cheapest new car in America right now, which also happens to be a Hyundai, the Venue. That’s for the Standard Edition. Upping the spend to 129,900 yuan ($19,300) gets the Smart Driving Edition, while 139,900 yuan ($20,800) buys the Long Range model, Auto Home reports. Those are some startling numbers when viewed from America or Europe, and remind us how cutthroat the competition is in the Chinese car market. Related: Police Are Slipping Warning Cards Under Hyundai And Kia Wipers Again The Ioniq V is a China-focused model developed under Beijing Hyundai, and despite what the prices suggest, it’s no cramped subcompact. At 4,900 mm (193 inches) long with a 2,900 mm (114-inch) wheelbase, it occupies roughly the same footprint as a Hyundai Sonata or a Toyota Camry. The Sonata measures 193.3 inches long on a 111.8-inch wheelbase; the Camry 193.5 inches on a 111.2-inch wheelbase. The Ioniq V wraps frameless doors and fastback proportions around some properly cyberpunk styling, and the paint chart runs eight colors deep, well past the silvers and grays Western buyers get stuck with. Cyber Gold, Gamma Green and a funky Dimensional Purple are all on the list. Inside, there’s a vast 27-inch 4K display running Qualcomm’s Snapdragon 8295 chip, plus a head-up display. Hyundai has also thrown Chinese AI models from Baidu and ByteDance into the infotainment system, while Momenta supplies the driver-assistance technology. Hyundai’s site additionally boasts nine airbags and extensive active safety equipment. Power comes from a single electric motor with either 188 hp (191 PS / 140 kW) or 225 hp (228 PS / 178 kW). CATL supplies 53.5 kWh and 66.8 kWh LFP batteries, producing four claimed CLTC ranges spanning 323 to 404 miles (520 to 650 km). Those optimistic Chinese-cycle numbers don’t translate directly into equivalent EPA range, naturally, but even if they’re 20 percent lower the value proposition is difficult to ignore. There’s no guarantee the Ioniq V will ever reach Western showrooms, much less at anything resembling Chinese pricing. Or that Hyundai will ever create the N version to capitalize on that Lamborghini-esque design, even though our own renders suggest it would look fantastic. But $17,800 for a brand-new electric sedan this stylish sounds like a great deal whichever side of the Pacific you’re on. title: Auto review: 2026 Cadillac CT5-V Blackwing is proof that the funeral for fun was greatly exaggerated - The Derrick
content: Clear skies. Low 57F. Winds light and variable.. For an additional $8,090, the 2026 Cadillac CT5-V Blackwing can come with semi-aniline leather seats, with custom quilting and carbon fiber seatbacks, (Cadillac/TNS) The 2026 Cadillac CT5-V Blackwing can achieve 60 mph in 3.4 seconds with the automatic, 3.6 seconds with the manual. (Cadillac/TNS) The 2026 Cadillac CT5-V Blackwing offers a 6.2-liter V8 producing 668 horsepower and 659 pound-feet of torque. (Cadillac/TNS) For an additional $8,090, the 2026 Cadillac CT5-V Blackwing can come with semi-aniline leather seats, with custom quilting and carbon fiber seatbacks, (Cadillac/TNS) The 2026 Cadillac CT5-V Blackwing can achieve 60 mph in 3.4 seconds with the automatic, 3.6 seconds with the manual. (Cadillac/TNS) The 2026 Cadillac CT5-V Blackwing offers a 6.2-liter V8 producing 668 horsepower and 659 pound-feet of torque. (Cadillac/TNS) The luxury sedan is supposed to be extinct. The industry has held the memorial service, lowered the casket, and handed out little sandwiches to the mourners. Thankfully for everyone who enjoys driving, Cadillac forgot to attend. Instead, it built the CT5-V Blackwing: a four-door luxury sedan with the temperament of a disgruntled executive who has discovered that the company wellness seminar is actually about feelings. This is not a vehicle designed by people who believe the automotive future is a silent pod carrying commuters between approved lifestyle zones. The Blackwing is built around an old-fashioned idea that a car should occasionally make you grin like an idiot. It has a supercharged V-8, available manual transmission, and enough performance capability to make you question whether the engineers were given a budget or simply left unsupervised. It starts with Cadillac’s CT5 midsize sedan, a vehicle that looks more like an old Nissan than a new Cadillac. Then it adds the usual go-fast dross attached to modern-day sports sedans. But the overall effect plays into the CT5’s adrenaline-fueled style, signaling its seriousness as a nuclear track weapon. Certainly, GM has loaded it with its best performance goodies. The test car was fitted with the $18,000 Precision Package, a collection of hardware and software upgrades aimed squarely at extracting maximum performance on the track. The package adds stiffer front springs, revised bushings, a larger front stabilizer bar, and unique front steering knuckles and rear toe links to achieve a more aggressive track-focused alignment. Stopping power comes courtesy of Brembo carbon-ceramic brakes, which deliver enormous bite while resisting fade during repeated high-speed track sessions. Their job is made easier by a set of ultra-high-performance Michelin Pilot Sport Cup 2 R tires, essentially racing rubber with just enough street manners to avoid requiring its own trailer. The package also includes recalibrated software systems, with retuned MagneRide dampers, steering, the electronic limited-slip differential (eLSD), and Performance Traction Management (PTM) all optimized to work with the sharper suspension setup and increased tire grip. The result is a CT5-V Blackwing that feels less like a fast luxury sedan and more like a road-legal track weapon that happens to have a back seat. At the heart of the Blackwing is a supercharged 6.2-liter V-8 producing 668 horsepower and 659 pound-feet of torque. It’s large, powerful, and gloriously out of step with the modern obsession with making every object behave like a sensible appliance. A washing machine does not need character. A car with a V-8 and an available manual gearbox does. And that gearbox matters. In an age where many cars are trying to remove the driver from the driving experience, preferably while adding another touchscreen, Cadillac hands you the controls and has you participate. It’s inconvenient, occasionally awkward, and vastly more rewarding than clicking a button and waiting for the car to decide you have earned acceleration privileges. Power goes to the rear wheels, and buyers can choose a 10-speed automatic if they wish. The manual is the enthusiast’s choice, which is another way of saying it’s the choice made by people who enjoy adding unnecessary effort to something a computer could technically do faster. These are also the people who still own mechanical watches, and get up to switch the TV channel. The Blackwing’s acceleration is dramatic, with 60 mph coming in 3.4 seconds with the automatic, 3.6 seconds with the manual. But the experience is more impressive than the stopwatch. The engine does not simply produce power; it announces its availability. The throttle response, the exhaust note, and the sensation of the rear tires negotiating with physics all combine into something that feels increasingly rare: a car with a fun personality. The chassis is equally serious. The CT5-V Blackwing uses Cadillac’s performance expertise to deliver sharp handling, strong braking capability, and a level of composure that allows the car to transition from comfortable highway cruiser to enthusiastic back-road weapon without requiring a personality transplant from the driver. That dual nature is the Blackwing’s greatest trick. It can behave like a premium sedan when you need to pretend that you’re a responsible adult. Then, with a conveniently empty stretch of road, it can remind you that the automotive engineers involved clearly had some unresolved issues with moderation. The remarkable thing is that the Blackwing is not merely a fast sedan wearing a luxury badge. It’s a genuinely sophisticated machine that can carry you through daily life without making you feel like you have purchased a very expensive punishment device. Inside, the Blackwing provides the expected luxury appointments and technology. Pop for the $8,090 semi-aniline leather seats with custom quilting and carbon fiber seatbacks and you’ll be treated to seriously sporty, and form thrones that provide all-day comfort and support without feeling punishing. Overall, it feels as posh as expected, despite a notoriously cheap lower door trim panel. Yet the main attraction is not the number of screens, electronic conveniences. Or its new for 2026 Performance Data Recorder. The highlight is the fact that Cadillac still built a car where the driver is part of the process rather than a passenger supervising the software. There are compromises. Fuel economy is not the Blackwing’s hobby. Rear-seat space is useful but not limousine-like. And despite its impressive capability, the sedan market is shrinking, meaning this car exists in a category that has been abandoned by many manufacturers in favor of taller vehicles that make everyone feel like they are commanding a small apartment building. But that is precisely why the CT5-V Blackwing matters. It’s not practical in the way a crossover is practical. It’s not efficient in the way an electric vehicle is efficient. It is not anonymous in the way so many modern luxury cars have become. It’s a machine built around the radical idea that driving should be entertaining. Van den Berg will miss the opening weeks of the campaign due to a groin issue after an interrupted pre-season. “Sepp has a groin issue,” Andrews explained. “We’ve had to manage that in a certain way.
