title: Ream v. US Department of the Treasury Brief: Restore the Original Meaning of the Commerce Clause - Cato Institute
content: Sign up to have blog posts delivered straight to your inbox! A former aerospace engineer and current homebrewer, Ohioan John Ream wants to distill spirits at home to enjoy with his wife. He would gladly register a still and pay the relevant federal tax, but an 1868 federal law prohibits home distilling. Operating a still in your home—or on a parcel “connected with” it—is a federal felony. Ream sued the government, alleging that this ban violates the Constitution. The Sixth Circuit upheld the ban as a necessary and proper means of enforcing the federal tax on distilled spirits, thereby breaking with a Fifth Circuit decision issued just 11 days earlier. Cato filed an amicus brief urging the Supreme Court to review Ream’s case and reverse the decision. Americans distilled spirits on their homesteads well before independence. Colonial Americans enjoyed drinking rum and grain whiskey, and by 1770, New England alone had over 150 distilleries. Prominent Founders, including George Washington, operated successful distilleries on their homesteads. Yet today, the federal government has banned home distilling outright. Ream is right that this ban exceeds Congress’s constitutional powers. In James Madison’s words, “The powers delegated by the … Constitution to the federal government are few and defined.” Congress possesses only those powers enumerated in the Constitution. Yet over time, judicial expansion of the commerce clause and the necessary and proper clause has transformed a limited power to regulate interstate trade into a sweeping license to regulate nearly all human activity—and even inactivity. The result is a national police power untethered from the Constitution’s original understanding and incompatible with the liberty-preserving structure it established. The original public meaning of the commerce clause was that Congress could regulate the trade and transportation of goods and people across state lines. It did not convey authority to control or prohibit purely intrastate activity such as home distilling. Unfortunately, the Supreme Court has strayed from that original understanding. In the New Deal–era case Wickard v. Filburn, the Court held that the commerce clause authorizes Congress to regulate even a farmer’s growing and consuming wheat entirely on his own farm. The Court reasoned that Congress may regulate local activities if, in the aggregate, they exert a substantial economic effect on interstate commerce. In the 2005 decision Gonzales v. Raich, the Court extended Wickard’s reasoning further, upholding the federal prohibition on the private, intrastate cultivation and use of marijuana. The majority first concluded that the plaintiffs’ marijuana activities were “economic.” It further held that courts need not determine whether regulated activities actually substantially affect interstate commerce in the aggregate, but only whether Congress had a “rational basis” for concluding that they do. Raich is the apex of congressional authority to regulate intrastate activity. It is time to restore the Constitution’s first principle of limited national power and overturn Raich. This case presents an ideal vehicle. By extending federal criminal law to purely in-home, noncommercial activity, the decision below collapses the distinction between national and state authority and erases structural limits that preserve federalism. The Constitution does not require another century of overreach—it demands fidelity to its text and original design. The Court should grant the petition for a writ of certiorari, overrule Raich, and reaffirm that federal powers are both enumerated and limited. Every weekday morning: independent analysis grounded in individual liberty, limited government, free markets, and peace.

title: Prima Facie Is Not the End of the Analysis: Gabriel v. Top 8 Construction (via Passle) - Ropers Majeski
content: When the injured worker is the only witness to his own fall and the record holds two versions of it, based on credible evidence, he does not get summary judgment under Labor Law 240(1). The Second Department reaffirmed that last week. In Gabriel v Top 8 Constr. Corp. (2026), an electrician's helper fell from a six-foot A-frame ladder while running a cable through an open-framed ceiling. He moved for partial summary judgment before discovery closed. Kings County denied the motion, adhered on reargument, and the Second Department affirmed. The Court agreed that the plaintiff made his prima facie showing. Testimony that the ladder "suddenly shook," causing him to fall, was enough on its own. Defendants still beat it. They raised a triable issue on sole proximate cause, and where "credible evidence reveals differing versions of the accident, one under which defendants would be liable and another under which they would not, questions of fact exist, making summary judgment inappropriate." What defeated the motion is significant. The employer produced a foreman's affidavit recounting the plaintiff's own statement that he had set two ladder feet on a piece of drywall. Plaintiff's own post-accident photographs showed the drywall. A safety engineer opined that a non-defective A-frame was an adequate device for the work.

title: VMAN 57: Belmont Cameli Is In Demand - V Magazine
content: After nearly a decade in the industry, the breakout Off Campus star is turning heads and opening doors After nearly a decade in the industry, the breakout Off Campus star is turning heads and opening doors When Belmont Cameli stepped into the skates of Off Campus’s Garrett Graham, he relied on Elle Kennedy’s novel of the same name more as guidance than scripture. He swapped literary Garrett’s penchant for Led Zeppelin with Arcade Fire (“That’s my version of the taste Garrett has,” he says), softening the literary character’s boisterous edges, concocting an all-too-easy-to-love student athlete with a true lived-in warmth. In his conversation with Grammy Award-winning singer-songwriter Laufey, it becomes increasingly clear what pumps the blood through Garrett’s beating heart: Cameli himself. Many fans first met the charismatic actor in 2020’s Saved by the Bell remake, but lacing up skates for Prime Video this year really plugged him into fancams and TikTok FYPs (including Laufey’s) globally. Amid his shooting schedule for Off Campus’s hotly awaited second season, Cameli sat down with Laufey to chat about Joshua Tree, ballet, and the necessity of leaning into fear. LAUFEY: I feel like I’ve been watching your star rise in the past few months, and it’s always so exciting to see artists, especially of different mediums, have their moment. And this is so, so deserved. BELMONT CAMELI: Yeah, for me too, watching you come up was probably the same feeling. L: I’m so excited to talk to you, because we met before. I feel like I ran into you one time at a party or something, or I feel like you were with your mom. BC: I think we ran into each other at the Melrose Flea or like the Silver Lake Flea—at a flea market. L: That does check out. So are you still living in LA? BC: Not really. I was in Laurel Canyon for a while, and then I moved out last fall, and now I don’t really have a lease anywhere. I’ve just been kind of bouncing around, but I spend the summers here in Vancouver, which is nice. L: You’ve been filming [Off Campus] in Vancouver, right? BC: Yeah, so we’re here for five months during the summers, and then I just kind of bounce around—mostly New York and LA—when I’m not working. L: Where do you go when you want to unwind? I definitely have that one place that I go to, and I just want to reset and forget about the industry. BC: Home definitely does that for me. When I’m in LA, it’s Joshua Tree. I usually make a point to go out there a couple of times a year with a small group of friends. I like to get, like, a shitty Airbnb, ideally with a bunch of desert garbage kind of around because that’s a theme out there. That’s my retreat, and then I also go to Mount Baldy, which is an hour east of L.A. It’s a really quite high summit, and there’s this little lodge, Mount Baldy Lodge, that’s kind of trapped in the ’70s, and it’s really a great drive. It’s a great hike, and it’s just a nice place to get away. L: I hear from a lot of people that when they go to Joshua Treats, it’s a very spiritual experience. Do you feel a connection with a higher power there? I don’t know. BC: There’s something about the sound of the desert. It’s so quiet out there, and the echo is so pronounced. You can have a conversation in a normal normal talking volume with somebody who’s super far away. Sound just travels differently in the desert. I’ve certainly had some spiritual experiences out there. L: I think especially when you’re an artist, having that go-to where you know you can connect to something beyond is very [important]. It’s a little woo woo, but I kind of love it. So, my next question. You are truly the man of the moment right now, and I feel like all my friends are talking about you, and you’re all over my FYP and everything. BC: I think for me, it’s weird to say that I feel cut out for it because it’s certainly been weird and hard in certain cases, just because of this sudden nature of it. It’s not that I was ever hoping to be famous, but I always wanted to have success in this career and understood that that would be a facet or symptom of the work. The biggest thing that’s changed for me has been that the number on the app on my phone has gone up. You know what I mean? But my reality is that the things I can see with my eyes are all exactly the same. I’ve always been extremely wary to digest that type of hype. It’s been a bit of an adjustment. I think the biggest thing I’ve noticed is—like, I was in New York last weekend, and one of my favorite things to do is just walk all day long, go get 15,000 steps, and that was a little more challenging. Honestly, I had a kind of sad moment resigning to that anonymity after a day spent out in New York of like, ‘Oh man, I can’t just enjoy the solitude of being in a big world as much as I used to.’ But people are always really nice; they enjoy the thing that I’ve worked really hard on. So that’s really sweet. I still feel very much like the same person, and the best part is now I’ll hopefully have some more opportunities on the other side of this, which is what I care about: the work. L: It seems like you have a healthy outlook on it and a good head on your shoulders. BC: I’m not on the internet like that, which is super helpful. BC: It’s terrible. I think when people say something nice, if that makes you feel good, then people have this same power to make you feel bad when they say something mean and rude. So I try not to ingest either. L: What I’ve been thinking a lot about this year is how I’ve done all these tours and written this music, and I know what it’s like to do these things, so I want to try things that scare me a little bit. I was like, ‘Should I jump out of a plane?’ But then I was like, ‘I really don’t want to jump out of a plane.’ Does anything scare you? BC: Oh my god, all the time. But that’s kind of my favorite. A lot of the greatest growth I’ve achieved as a person and an artist has been on the other side of things that scared me the most. My instrument is my brain and my body. That’s what I had to continually fine-tune, and that’s a never-ending process. The more life experience I have, the more I have to pull from, and having a range of experiences is really important. So I never neglect things that scare me. Those are the most essential parts of life. When I can apply those to the work, that’s where the fulfillment comes from. But yeah, I’ve done a lot of things that scare me—leaving school in the first place to become an actor was kind of horrifying. But it’s no fun to do something that isn’t challenging. L: I heard that on top of being an actor, you are also a filmmaker, and that’s something you want to be a part of your journey. What inspires you? What kind of stories do you want to tell? BC: There’s a lot I want to do right now. I’m focused on building out my body of work as an actor, but I can’t wait to direct. When I write, comedy flows from me the most naturally, so I look forward to working on comedy. I’ve always been a big fan of both blockbuster comedies and niche, offbeat comedies. L: There hasn’t been enough of that in the past couple of years. So you’ll bring that back. BC: I completely agree. I mean, that was the heartbeat of my fan experience as a kid, all these big Steve Carell, Will Ferrell, and Jim Carrey [movies]. I agree there could and should be more of them. I love comedy. It’s my favorite. I grew up as a student of Robin Williams, David Letterman, and these comedy legends. Norm Macdonald was one of my favorite standups. These people I revere. I also really want to write a drama about ballet because my sister was a ballerina, and I’ve always been appreciative of that art form as an audience member. It would be a great challenge athletically. I’ve gotten to play different types of athletes now, and I think it would be really fulfilling. The things they do in their movement and as athletes are fascinating. The life of a ballerina is usually pretty unglamorous and very difficult, so that’s a story I would love to tell someday. We’ll see. L: That’s super cool. If you need someone to score it or work on music, you know exactly who to call now. This cover story appears in the pages of VMAN 57: now available for purchase! title: GAMPER PREVIEW | FC Barcelona Femení v Brighton & Hove Albion Women - FC Barcelona
content: The Estadí Johan Cruyff is set to come alive once again as today is the 5th women's Festa del Gamper Estrella Damm. The traditional curtain raiser to the upcoming season sees FC Barcelona Femení host English team Brighton & Hove Albion Women. The gates at the Estadí Johan Cruyff will open at 6.30pm CEST. The Barça Femení squad for the 2026/27 season will be presented from 7.00pm CEST and then the match itself kicks off at 8.00pm CEST. Both events can be watched live on Barça Play and the Club's YouTube channel, except for in the United Kingdom. First team player Renee Van Asten has a right thigh strain and will miss the match today. Pere Romeu has named the following squad for the 5th women's Festa del Gamper Estrella Damm: Gemma Font, Irene Paredes, Sydney Schertenleib, Kerolin Nicoli, Marta Torrejón, Claudia Pina, Caroline Graham, Patri Guijarro, Cata Coll, Ewa Pajor, Vicky López, Carla Julià, Esmee Brugts, Aïcha Cámara, Martina Fernández, Tyler McCamey, Julia Torres, Rosalía, Carolina, Ohlander, Mayssa and Elena. New additions always generate a lot of excitement of course, and this Gamper is no exception. It will be the first time for McCamey, Kerolin and Van Asten (who misses the match). It will be a third Gamper for Martina Fernández after she played in the 23/24 and 24/25 editions. The Catalan is back at the Club for her second spell after a season and a half at English club Everton. The official presentation will also see the coach and captain say a few words as is tradition. This will be the third Gamper at the helm for Pere Romeu, while Patri Guijarro will take to the mic for the first time as first captain. In addition to the official squad presentation and the subsequent Gamper match, fans present at the Estadí Johan Cruyff will be able to enjoy a performance by Mallorca singer Maria Jaume at halftime. All set for a special evening for FC Barcelona fans to enjoy football, presentations and more to welcome in the new season.

title: Hyundai Ioniq V starts pre-sales in China from $17,700 - CnEVPost
content: Beijing Hyundai, Hyundai Motor's joint venture in China, opened pre-sales for the Ioniq V at the 2026 Chengdu Auto Show, which kicked off on Friday, advancing the automaker's product offensive in the world's largest electric vehicle market. The Ioniq V is available in 3 variants, with pre-sales prices ranging from 119,900 yuan ($17,680) to 139,900 yuan, and is scheduled to officially launch in September. The 540 Max is priced at 119,900 yuan, the 540 Max+ at 129,900 yuan, and the 650 Max+ at 139,900 yuan. All 3 variants currently available for pre-sales are battery electric vehicles, offering a CLTC range of up to 650 km and supporting an 800-volt high-voltage fast-charging system. Previous information has indicated that the Ioniq V lineup may also add an extended-range electric vehicle (EREV) version in the future. The Ioniq V is the first production model from Hyundai's Ioniq brand in China and the production version of the Venus Concept unveiled at the Beijing Auto Show in April. The mid-size sedan was led throughout its development by Hyundai's China design center and tailored for Chinese consumers. Hyundai also plans to offer the model in overseas markets. The vehicle measures 4,900 mm in length, 1,890 mm in width and 1,470 mm in height, with a wheelbase of 2,900 mm. It features a fastback profile and frameless doors. The Ioniq V is based on Hyundai's E-GMP (Electric Global Modular Platform) and offers single-motor versions with maximum outputs of 140 kW and 168 kW. Its batteries are supplied by CATL (HKEX: 3750), using lithium iron phosphate (LFP) chemistry, with capacities of 53.5 kWh and 66.8 kWh. Smart features are another area where Beijing Hyundai has stepped up its focus for the Chinese market. The Ioniq V features a 27-inch 4K display, Qualcomm's Snapdragon 8295 chip and a head-up display. Its driver-assistance system was jointly developed by Beijing Hyundai and Momenta (HKEX: 6880), providing L2+ assisted-driving functions on highways. The vehicle's infotainment system also integrates AI models including Baidu's Ernie Bot and ByteDance's Doubao, highlighting Hyundai's growing use of Chinese technology suppliers. The rollout of the Ioniq V will serve as the first major market test of Hyundai's latest China strategy. Hyundai officially introduced the Ioniq brand to China in April and plans to launch 20 battery electric vehicle (BEV) and EREV models in the country over the next 5 years. The company aims to scale its China business to 500,000 units by 2030 through faster local development, deeper cooperation with Chinese suppliers and a new generation of electrified products.

title: Dr. David V. DiMarco - The Poughkeepsie Journal
content: Dr. David V. DiMarco, a life-long resident of Wappingers Falls, NY, died suddenly at his home on August 19, 2026 at the age of 71. He was born in Poughkeepsie, NY on February 23, 1955, son of the late Henry A. & Dolores L. DiMarco. He attended St. Mary’s School in Wappingers Falls and graduated from Our Lady of Lourdes High School in Poughkeepsie, class of 1973. He later went on to Union College and the University of Padua in Italy, ultimately graduating from Mount Sinai School of Medicine in 1981. David worked as an orthopedic surgeon for almost 40 years and was a founding partner of Orthopedic Associates of Dutchess County. After he retired from OADC in 2020, he came out of retirement to treat the Veterans at Castle Point. He was happiest caring for his patients - who called him “Doc” - while his colleagues called him “DVD.” He loved his work. When he was not treating patients, he was lifting weights, stalking the BMW lot for the newest M5, and adding to his endless tie collection. He also enjoyed the simple pleasures like anchovies and snacking on peanut M&Ms. His favorite activity was spending time with his family, listening and laughing to the same stories repeatedly. On October 9, 1983 in Orange, NJ, he married the love of his life, Shari M. Gilbert, who survives him at home. Along with his beloved wife, David is survived by his three daughters: Jaimee (Brian), Alexa (Zachary), and Erika; though we can’t forget about his granddog, ‘Shay.’ He is also survived by his four brothers, whom he affectionately referred to as Hank (#I), Larry (#3), Robert (#4), and Gerry (#5), and a host of nieces, nephews, friends & colleagues. He leaves behind a legacy of laughter, love and unmatched style. Rest Easy – you’ve earned the victory lap. His Family will receive Friends on Saturday, August 22 from 3:00 -7:00 pm at the DELEHANTY FUNERAL HOME, 64 E. Main St., Wappingers Falls, NY; where a Prayer Service and Remembrance will be offered at 7:00 pm. Interment will be private at the convenience of his family. In lieu of flowers, the family wishes for memorial donation to be made to either VA Hudson Valley HCS – Castle Point Campus, 41 Castle Point Rd., Wappingers Falls, NY 12590 or the American Heart Association, P.O. Box 840692 Dallas, TX 75284. To offer a message of condolence or share a fond memory of David, please visit: www.DelehantyFuneral.com Coping with grief when a traditional funeral isn't possible

title: V’s ‘Unmistakable Style’ and ‘Artistic Vision’ Helped Him Land New Champion Campaign - Rolling Stone
content: If you purchase an independently reviewed product or service through a link on our website, Rolling Stone may receive an affiliate commission. ARMY have long known that BTS’ V was a champ, whether he was pouring his heart out on his solo album, serving his country in the military, or pushing the limits in the gym. But now, Kim Taehyung makes it official with a new partnership with Champion, the iconic American athletic and sportswear brand. V stars as the face of the brand’s “True Champion” campaign, which celebrates “the people shaping today’s culture through their originality, perspective and enduring impact,” per a release. The singer is seen posing for a series of photographs showing off Champion’s signature sweats while debuting some new streetwear-inspired looks for the brand as well. Though the campaign images were released Aug. 10, the pieces V was wearing weren’t available to purchase online until now. Some of the pieces are only available in Korea, China or Japan, extending V’s reach as Champion’s global ambassador. However, we’ve rounded up some of the items that are available to purchase here in the U.S. This cotton blend sweatshirt features collegiate-inspired styling and a unique snap neck closure that can either be kept open like a polo collar or buttoned up for a mockneck look. A “Champion” script applique with raw edge is splashed across the chest, with an embroidered “C” patch on the left sleeve. V sports this long sleeve rugby-style top in a “tiger lily” colorway. We like the contrast-color polo collar and ribbed trim. There is an embroidered Champion script patch at the chest and a workwear label on the corner, just above the hem. Three other colors are available in sizes small to 2XL. Part of Champion’s “reverse weave” collection, which features heavyweight sweats with a worn-in look and feel, this hoodie features a contrast color drawstring, large front pouch pockets and a subtle “C” logo patch on the sleeve.This one is available in a classic fit, though you can size up if you want that trendy, oversized look. You can also find a full-zip version for $40 at Target. V tops off his look in this photo with a corduroy baseball cap that features both the Champion script logo and capital “C” logo embroidered on the front.The classic hat features a five-panel construction with a relaxed, “dad hat”-style fit. The back is adjustable.V paired the hat with a black Champion script sweatshirt (you can find a similar version for just $23 here). The singer’s Champion varsity jacket seen at right is currently only available in Asia, but you can find his baggy sweatpants online through Farfetch. The cotton sweats feature an elastic waistband, open hem, and the iconic C logo at the left hip.You can also find similar relaxed-fit sweatpants in a lighter “silver heather” colorway on the Champion site for just $37 here. Choose from sizes small to 2XL. And find a similar maroon Champion varsity jacket on Amazon here. Champion says V was a perfect fit for the new campaign, citing his “unmistakable style, artistic vision and global reach” in a press release. And while he’s best known as a singer, the brand says his influence “extends beyond music, leaving an indelible mark across fashion, art and popular culture while connecting with millions of fans worldwide.” “True Champion represents a new chapter for Champion and the values that continue to define our brand,” says Stefani Fleurant, executive vice president, Marketing, Sport & Lifestyle at Authentic. “V’s creative vision, global influence and genuine connection with his audience make him a natural partner for Champion.” V joins fellow musicians Sofi Tukker, model Romeo Beckham, basketball star Kyle Kuzma, and U.S. women’s hockey player Megan Keller in the new campaign, among others.
